VERIFICATION LIMITS: WebFetch could not reach iea.org, yolegroup.com or lightwaveonline.com, and curl to sec.gov was refused by the proxy. These hosts must be allowed in the session's network settings to read the pages directly. All figures here were checked against search-result excerpts of the cited URLs, not full page reads. CIKs were taken from the sec.gov EDGAR URLs returned by search: COHR 820318, LITE 1633978, CRDO 1807794, AAOI 1158114, FN 1408710, GLW 24741, POET 1437424 (20-F filer), VRT 1674101, ETN 1551182, POWL 80420, NVT 1720635, MOD 67347, INV 2001557, KLIC 56978. The NASDAQ:INV ticker for Innventure was not confirmed in this pass.

SCHEMA GAP: This schema has no fields for revenue, FCF or cash runway, so a few sourced revenue figures are in the thesis text. No FCF or runway figures were computed. AAOI (GAAP loss reported in Q3 2026, though sources conflict) and POET (development-stage) are the names that need a runway calculation from their 10-Q / 6-K cash and operating cash flow.

GROWTH ESTIMATES: The Dell'Oro July 2026 forecast ($120B DCPI by 2030, 22% CAGR) supersedes its Feb 2026 forecast (>$80B, mid-teens) and its July 2025 forecast ($63.1B by 2029, 15%). Do not merge vintages. Yole's back-end equipment 2026 edition (2026-2031: TCB 7%, hybrid bonding 23.4%) supersedes the 2025 edition used above. Sources conflict on that edition's total-market CAGR (6.3% vs 4.4%). LightCounting gives no verifiable 2030 dollar total. TrendForce's CPO/NPO >$39B by 2030 and Yole's $112.3B 2031 optical transceiver figures use different definitions and were not included.

STRUCTURAL EVENTS: Celestial AI was acquired by Marvell (closed 2026-02-02) and LiquidStack by Trane (Mar 2026), so both are excluded as startups. Marvell announced the acquisition of Lumentum on 2026-11-02 (all-stock, close expected 1H 2028), which changes LITE's 10-bagger profile. Cerebras reportedly IPO'd in May 2026; this is unverified and it was excluded. Etched ($500M at $5B per EE Times Japan) has no identified public holder and was excluded.

STARTUP CAVEATS: Lightmatter has an unverified April 2026 S-1 claim from a low-reliability aggregator. Forge and Nasdaq Private Market show it as private, and the last primary round is the Oct 2024 Series D at $4.4B. Ayar Labs added a $150M extension on 2026-09-10; an aggregator implies >$5B post-money, which is not primary, so the $3.75B Series E valuation is kept. Accelsius: an aggregator cites ~$665M post-money and Dealroom $260M, so it is null. ZutaCore: Calcalist's ~$600M is an estimate, not company-stated, so it is null. Groq's $6.9B valuation predates the NVIDIA license; NVIDIA is a licensor, not a confirmed equity holder, and the reported $20B figure is unconfirmed. No stake percentages were found in any source for these startups, so pctOwned is null throughout. A sourced % does exist for a public company: Applied Materials' 9% stake in Besi (April 2025).

KOREA: Use DART quarterly reports to confirm figures for Hanmi (042700), Taihan Fiberoptics (010170, KOSDAQ) and the power trio. The trio's Q3 2026 combined numbers come from bizwatch citing DART. Taihan Fiberoptics' contract values come from ddaily/Hankyung reporting of its disclosures.

sectors.researchNotes:
SOURCING LIMITS
- WebFetch could not resolve ifr.org, goldmansachs.com or morganstanley.com in this session; those hosts must be allowed in the network settings. I did not fetch any page from sec.gov.
- Every figure therefore comes from WebSearch snippets of the cited pages, not from reading the full documents. Re-verify before publishing.

CIKs
- Confirmed from sec.gov EDGAR URLs in search results: ISRG 1035267, TER 97210, SYM 1837240, PRCT 1588978, SERV 1832483, RR 1963685, OUST 1816581.
- NVDA 0001045810 and TSLA 0001318605 come from prior knowledge, not confirmed in this session.
- AGLT (post-SPAC entity) CIK is unknown and set to null.

STATUS CHANGES SINCE THE STARTING HINTS
- Unitree is no longer private. It listed on the SSE STAR Market as 688836 on 2026-08-19.
- Agility Robotics is no longer private. It closed its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI on 2026-11-04 and trades as NASDAQ:AGLT.
- SoftBank agreed on 2025-10-08 to buy ABB's robotics division for US$5.375bn, with closing expected mid-to-late 2026. I found no closing confirmation. ABB is not listed for that reason.
- Hyundai Motor Group affiliates are buying SoftBank's ~9.65% Boston Dynamics stake for ~US$325M. The Boston Dynamics percentages are the pre-deal split reported by Herald Corp, and closing is unconfirmed.

VALUATIONS
- Apptronik: the company release (2026-02-11) did not disclose a valuation. Bloomberg reported "more than $5.5bn" and TechCrunch ~US$5.3bn, so valuationUsd is set to null.
- Skild AI: Bloomberg reported "above $14bn" (2026-01-14). The 14000000000 entered is that floor.
- Physical Intelligence: US$5.6bn is the last confirmed round (Nov 2025). A 2026 round at ~US$11bn+ was reported as in talks, with no confirmed close found.
- Figure AI: US$39bn (Sept 2025) is the last confirmed round. Bloomberg reported 2026 talks at US$39.5bn, with no confirmed close found.
- 1X: last confirmed round is the Jan 2024 Series B, valuation undisclosed. A reported raise of up to US$1bn at US$10bn+ is not confirmed.
- NEURA: US$7bn is reported only. Earlier rounds conflict (Mar 2026 ~US$4.6bn per Caproasia).
- Sanctuary AI: no disclosed current valuation.

STAKES
- No public-company % stake was found for Figure, Apptronik, Skild, Physical Intelligence, 1X, Sanctuary or NEURA. pctOwned is null and no % was computed.
- Disclosed %s: Samsung–Rainbow Robotics 35% (Samsung newsroom), LG–Bear Robotics 51% (LG press release), LG Electronics–Robotis ~6.6% (reported; other figures 6.56% and 7.3%).
- Samsung and LG also back Figure and Skild through venture arms according to some coverage. I did not include those holdings because I did not verify them.

GROWTH ESTIMATES
- The six growth estimates use different definitions and are not comparable: IFR = industrial robot installations; Goldman = humanoid TAM in 2035; Morgan Stanley = humanoid market including supply chain and services in 2050; BofA = humanoid unit shipments. Do not merge them.
- The Goldman 2026 revision (~US$138bn, 6.48M units) appears only in secondary coverage.
- BofA's 86% CAGR is as reported by press coverage of the note.
- IFR's 7% CAGR is IFR's own stated 2026–2029 rate.

PUBLIC-COMPANY DATA QUALITY
- Richtech Robotics has a June 2026 8-K saying its FY2024 and FY2025 financials should no longer be relied on and will be restated.
- Doosan Robotics financials come from aggregators and conflict with each other. Verify against DART.

OMITTED
- Fanuc, Yaskawa, ABB, Hiwin and Samsung (KRX:005930) are not in the public list. For the Japanese and Taiwanese names, no primary source URL was retrieved in this session.

cases.name: Rigetti Computing
cases.startRevenue: $12.0M FY2023; Q4 2023 revenue $3.4M vs $6.1M in Q4 2022 (release 2024-03)
cases.catalysts: Novera QPU sales (including to AFRL) and the UK NQCC 24-qubit system win. Sector sentiment shock in Dec 2024 drove a speculative re-rating.
cases.preconditions: Deeply loss-making: FY2023 operating loss $72.3M, net loss $75.1M. Cash and AFS securities $99.9M at 2023-12-31, a short runway at that loss rate before later equity raises. Revenue was shrinking. Basis: primary (Rigetti IR).

cases.name: D-Wave Quantum
cases.catalysts: Annealing-based commercial QCaaS bookings growth and the quantum sector re-rating in late 2024.
cases.preconditions: Tiny revenue base, heavy losses, reliance on equity issuance. Bought at a trough below $1 per share (pipeline to verify). Basis: primary (D-Wave IR).

cases.name: Rocket Lab
cases.catalysts: Space Systems (satellite buses and components) and defense constellation contracts, the Neutron medium-lift program, and launch cadence recovery after the Sept 2023 anomaly. Backlog was $1,046.1M at 2023-12-31 (10-K).
cases.preconditions: Loss-making, with revenue growth slowed to 16% after the launch anomaly. Raised $355M in convertible notes. Backlog was large relative to revenue. Basis: primary (company release / 10-K).

cases.name: Celestica
cases.catalysts: Hyperscaler networking switches (400G/800G) and custom AI compute (HPS/ODM-like model) mix shift lifted margins and growth.
cases.preconditions: Profitable, low-margin EMS business: Q4 2022 non-IFRS operating margin 5.3%. Record non-IFRS margin and EPS in FY2022. Low starting valuation multiple. 2023 guidance at least $7.5B. Basis: primary (company release).

cases.name: Credo Technology
cases.catalysts: Active electrical cables (AECs) ramping at new hyperscale customers. FY2024 revenue $192.97M; about 3/4 of Q4 FY24 revenue was AI-driven; management expected an AEC inflection in H2 FY25 (FY24 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1807794/000162828024025607/credoq42024ex-991.htm).
cases.preconditions: Small cap with a GAAP net loss (FY2023 net loss about $16.55M per MarketScreener summary; secondary). A customer-concentration guide-down left revenue temporarily declining at the start. High gross margin (FY23 non-GAAP about 58%). Basis: primary (SEC Ex.99.1) plus secondary for the net loss.

cases.name: AppLovin
cases.catalysts: AXON 2.0 machine-learning ad engine (2023) drove a sharp acceleration in software-platform revenue and margins, then the expansion into e-commerce advertising.
cases.preconditions: GAAP net loss of $193M in FY2022, but FCF positive at $388.0M and adjusted EBITDA above $1B (38% margin). A depressed multiple after the post-IPO collapse. Basis: primary (10-K).

cases.name: Bloom Energy
cases.catalysts: On-site, behind-the-meter fuel-cell power for AI data centers facing grid interconnection delays (utility and hyperscaler/infrastructure-partner agreements in 2024-2025).
cases.preconditions: GAAP operating loss $208.9M in FY2023; non-GAAP operating profit $19.2M; non-GAAP gross margin 25.8%; Q4 2023 revenue -22.8% YoY. 2024 guidance $1.4B-$1.6B. Basis: primary (company IR).

cases.name: Oklo
cases.catalysts: Listed via the AltC SPAC merger (closed 2024-05-09). Advanced-reactor (SMR) policy support and data-center power framework agreements. A thematic re-rating of nuclear in 2025.
cases.preconditions: Pre-revenue. FY2024 net cash used in operating activities $38.4M (10-K). Net loss $73.6M and cash plus marketable securities $275.3M at 2024-12-31 (secondary coverage). 2025 operating cash-use guidance $65M-$80M. Basis: primary 10-K for cash use; secondary for net loss and cash.

cases.name: Enphase Energy
cases.catalysts: Restructuring and cost cuts, IQ microinverter gross-margin expansion, and a return to non-GAAP profitability in Q4 2017. The residential solar plus storage cycle followed.
cases.preconditions: Near-distress: Q4 2017 GAAP operating loss $2.1M, non-GAAP operating income $1.3M, cash about $29.1M. Revenue declining. Basis: primary (10-K / Q4 2017 release). Instructive because the stock later round-tripped a large part of the gain (not sourced here).

cases.name: Celsius Holdings (non-sector control)
cases.catalysts: US distribution expansion and fitness-energy category share gains; later a PepsiCo distribution deal. Included to show that a tenfold run needs growth acceleration on a small base, not a particular sector.
cases.preconditions: Small base, accelerating revenue, gross profit +49% to $31.3M. Net income to common $10.0M, including a $12.5M one-off Asia gain. Basis: primary (SEC Ex.99.1).

cases.name: Plug Power (cautionary)
cases.startRevenue: FY2019 gross billings $236.8M (a billings metric, not GAAP revenue), per the Q4 2019 shareholder letter
cases.catalysts: Hydrogen and green-policy theme (2020), forklift fuel-cell customer wins, and a positive adjusted EBITDA year as described by the company.
cases.preconditions: GAAP loss-making with negative gross margin in Q1 2019 ($(6.8)M, per Q1 2019 release). Equity-funded. Basis: primary (SEC 8-K). Cautionary: the 10x was driven by the theme without FCF; the later reversal was not sourced here.

cases.name: Micron Technology
cases.startRevenue: $37.38B FY2025 (FYE Aug 2025) vs $25.11B FY2024; Q4 FY25 revenue $11.32B (release 2025-09-23)
cases.catalysts: HBM ramp (Q4 FY25 HBM revenue near $2B, secondary) and an AI-driven DRAM/NAND supply shortage. Market cap first topped $1T on 2026-05-26 (Reuters via secondary). The stock later retreated from a late-June 2026 peak above $1,200 (Barchart).
cases.preconditions: Already profitable at a cyclical recovery point: FY2025 operating cash flow $17.53B; Q1 FY26 gross-margin guidance 51.5% ±1.0%. A mega cap that still 10x'd thanks to a memory supercycle. Basis: primary (SEC Ex.99.1, via search extract) plus secondary for HBM and market cap.
cases.drawdownsDuringRun: Retreated from a late-June 2026 peak above $1,200 (Barchart, 2026; secondary)

cases.name: Sandisk
cases.catalysts: Spun off from Western Digital in Feb 2025. NAND price upcycle driven by AI inference and enterprise SSD demand. Secondary reports describe a gain of several thousand percent from the April 2025 low (e.g., Stacker, May 2026: about $30 to about $1,447).
cases.preconditions: GAAP net loss of $1.641B in FY2025, including a $1.83B goodwill impairment. Gross margin recovering (30.1% vs 16.1%). An orphaned spin-off at a cyclical trough. Basis: primary (company release).

cases.name: Western Digital
cases.catalysts: Pure-play HDD after the Sandisk separation; cloud was 90% of revenue. AI data-lake capacity demand; HDD output reportedly sold out for 2026 (secondary). Deleveraging ($2.6B debt reduction), new dividend, $2.0B buyback.
cases.preconditions: Profitable and FCF positive (Q4 FY25 FCF $675M). A capacity-disciplined duopoly in HDD. Basis: primary (SEC Ex.99.1).

cases.name: Lumentum
cases.catalysts: Hyperscale AI optical components (EMLs, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth lasers) and optical transceivers. Management targeted more than $600M quarterly revenue by June 2026. Reported 1-year return of about 1,474% (NerdWallet, 2026; secondary).
cases.preconditions: Barely GAAP profitable: FY2025 GAAP net income $25.9M; non-GAAP net income $146.4M; non-GAAP operating margin 9.7%. Q4 FY25 Cloud & Networking +66.5% YoY, i.e. revenue was accelerating at the start. Basis: primary (company IR).

cases.name: SK hynix
cases.startMarketCap: About $100B (reported 'from $100 billion to $1 trillion in 16 months', Invezz 2026-05-27; secondary)
cases.startRevenue: ₩66.19T FY2024; operating profit ₩23.47T (35% margin vs -24% in 2023)
cases.catalysts: HBM leadership (HBM sales >4.5x in 2024; HBM >40% of Q4 2024 DRAM revenue), HBM3E/HBM4 supply to NVIDIA, and the 2025-26 memory price surge. Market cap hit ₩1,680T (about $1.12T) on 2026-05-27 (https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/5/29/south-koreas-sk-hynix-enters-exclusive-1-trillion-club).
cases.preconditions: Profits had just recovered from a 2023 loss year. Bottleneck supplier (lead HBM vendor). The start valuation ignored HBM's structural margin. Basis: Korea Herald report of the company release (reported).

cases.name: EcoPro
cases.startRevenue: Consolidated 2022 sales ₩5.6397T, operating profit ₩613.2B (KED Global 2024-02-07; reported)
cases.catalysts: Retail ('Ants') buying of the cathode-material theme tied to IRA-era battery localization. Up 848% YTD by early July 2023 and passed ₩1M per share. Retail net buying was ₩1.42T from Jan 2 to Apr 19, 2023 (reported).
cases.preconditions: Holding company of EcoPro BM, profitable on record 2022 results. Valuation was stretched: Samsung Securities cited a premium of about 20% over the value of its subsidiary holdings, and Morgan Stanley said EcoPro BM's fair value was about half the price. Earnings halved in 2023 (KED). Basis: reported.
cases.drawdownsDuringRun: About -26% from peak in April 2023 after analyst warnings (reported)

cases.name: HD Hyundai Electric
cases.catalysts: US grid replacement cycle, a transformer shortage and AI/data-center load growth. Pricing power on high-voltage transformers. 2024 operating profit ₩669B, +112.2% YoY (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025012011045590430). Q1 2023 margin passed 8% for the first time since the 2017 spin-off.
cases.preconditions: Trough profitability: 2021 operating profit ₩9.7B, -87% YoY (Asia Business Daily, 2022-02-04). Near-breakeven, under-owned grid-equipment maker just before the supply shortage. Basis: reported.

cases.name: Hyosung Heavy Industries
cases.startRevenue: Consolidated 2023 revenue about ₩4.30T; operating profit about ₩257.8B vs about ₩143.2B in 2022 (company IR)
cases.catalysts: US 765kV ultra-high-voltage transformer demand; reportedly supplied nearly half of the 765kV units installed in the US. Memphis plant expansion from 130 to more than 250 units per year. Record backlog of ₩10.72T (+63%) at Q2 2025 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025072809270788265).
cases.preconditions: Profitable but low-margin conglomerate spin-off with leverage. Profit was inflecting (2023 operating profit vs 2022). Bottleneck in US extra-high-voltage transformers. Basis: primary (company IR page).

cases.name: Hanmi Semiconductor
cases.catalysts: Sole TC-bonder supplier for SK hynix HBM. The ₩41.5B 'Dual TC Bonder 1.0 Dragon' order (Sept 2023) was its largest ever, equal to 12.69% of 2022 revenue. Cumulative SK hynix orders reached ₩358.7B by June 2024 (https://amp.kedglobal.com/newsAmp/ked202406070008).
cases.preconditions: Revenue was falling at the start: 2023 sales about ₩159B and operating profit ₩34.5B (KED, July 2024) vs ₩327.6B 2022 sales. Orders and the bottleneck position led reported revenue. Later risk: second-sourcing to Hanwha Precision Machinery (2024), and Q1 2026 sales ₩50.9B (-65.5%), operating profit -87.9% (reported).

cases.name: Alteogen
cases.catalysts: On 2024-02-22 the Merck (MSD) license was amended to make ALT-B4 hyaluronidase exclusive for Keytruda SC: up to ₩575B, $20M upfront. Keytruda SC FDA approval in Sept 2025; royalties reportedly about 2% of net sales.
cases.preconditions: Platform-technology biotech, operating-loss-making in 2023 and dependent on milestones. Validation by a big-pharma partner on the world's top-selling drug was the key re-rating trigger. Basis: reported (Asia Business Daily).

cases.name: Rainbow Robotics
cases.catalysts: Samsung Electronics took a 10.22% stake via third-party allotment at ₩30,400 (Jan 2023), raised it to 14.99% (Mar 2023) with call options up to 59.94%, then exercised to 35% in Dec 2024 and consolidated it as a subsidiary. Price went from ₩34,450 at end-2022 to ₩120,700 by mid-March 2023. Surpassed ₩350,000 in Feb 2025 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025020509212617245).
cases.preconditions: Tiny revenue, roughly breakeven (2022 operating profit about ₩1.3B, aggregator). Humanoid and cobot platform. A strategic-acquirer option premium drove the run, not earnings. Basis: reported (KED Global).
cases.drawdownsDuringRun: Later fell to the ₩400,000 range, roughly half its peak (Herald, mbiz.heraldcorp.com/article/10856631; reported)

cases.name: Hanwha Aerospace
cases.catalysts: Post-Ukraine European rearmament. The 2022 Poland framework deals (K9 howitzers and Chunmoo) became export deliveries. 2023 operating profit ₩704.9B (+76%). Intraday peak ₩1,127,000 in 2025 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025101409580700456). Also has space and launch exposure.
cases.preconditions: Profitable industrial conglomerate at a low multiple before export orders. The order-backlog step change came from geopolitics. Q3 2026 operating profit -46% YoY (reported) shows the cycle risk. Basis: reported (Asia Business Daily).

patterns.pattern: Bottleneck supplier to a capex super-cycle: most growth-sector 10-baggers were the scarce input (chip, memory, packaging tool, transformer, cooling, cable) when demand broke out, not the end-application brand.
patterns.evidence: NVIDIA (sole scaled AI GPU, FY23 revenue flat at $26.97B at the start); SK hynix (lead HBM vendor, HBM >40% of Q4 2024 DRAM revenue); Hanmi (sole SK hynix TC-bonder supplier, ₩41.5B order = 12.69% of 2022 revenue); HD Hyundai Electric and Hyosung Heavy (US high-voltage transformer shortage; Hyosung reportedly about half of installed US 765kV units); Vertiv (record $4.8B backlog); Credo (AEC ramp); Lumentum (EML/pump lasers, Cloud & Networking +66.5% in Q4 FY25).

patterns.pattern: The run starts at a trough in reported earnings or a GAAP loss caused by the cycle or a one-off, not at peak earnings. Trailing P/E looked bad or meaningless at the start.
patterns.evidence: AMD FY2015 net loss $660M; SK hynix 2023 operating margin -24% before 35% in 2024; Sandisk FY2025 net loss $1.641B including a $1.83B goodwill impairment; Vistra 2021 net loss $1,264M (Winter Storm Uri); Constellation 2022 GAAP net loss $160M with $2,667M adjusted EBITDA; HD Hyundai Electric 2021 operating profit ₩9.7B (-87%).

patterns.pattern: Orders and backlog lead revenue. The stock re-rates on order or backlog evidence while reported revenue is flat or even falling.
patterns.evidence: Hanmi 2023 sales fell to about ₩159B from ₩327.6B in 2022 while SK hynix TC-bonder orders hit records; Vertiv backlog $4.8B (+49%) covering >70% of next-year guidance; Rocket Lab backlog $1,046.1M against $244.6M revenue; Hyosung backlog ₩10.72T (+63%); Credo Q4 FY23 revenue -14.5% YoY just before the AEC ramp.

patterns.pattern: A profitability or FCF inflection is often the trigger, and it opens up index eligibility and institutional ownership.
patterns.evidence: Palantir's first GAAP-profitable quarter in Q4 2022 ($31M), with FY22 adjusted FCF $203M; Tesla FY2019 FCF $1.1B; Enphase back to non-GAAP operating profit in Q4 2017 ($1.3M); AppLovin FCF $388.0M despite a $193M GAAP loss; Celsius profitable at $75.1M revenue.

patterns.pattern: Strategic validation by a mega-cap partner or a signature contract re-rates small and mid caps abruptly, especially in Korea.
patterns.evidence: Rainbow Robotics: Samsung 10.22% → 14.99% → 35% (price ₩34,450 end-2022 → ₩120,700 within about 2.5 months); Alteogen: exclusive Merck Keytruda SC amendment (up to ₩575B) in Feb 2024; Constellation: 20-year Microsoft PPA for the TMI restart (about 835 MW) in Sept 2024; Hanwha Aerospace: Poland K9/Chunmoo export program; Hanmi: SK hynix HBM orders.

patterns.pattern: Pre-revenue or tiny-revenue themes (quantum, SMR, hydrogen) can 10x fastest. Survival depends on cash runway and the ability to raise equity into strength, so runway is a gating screen.
patterns.evidence: IonQ: $11.1M revenue, $48.5M net loss, $537.8M cash (long runway); Rigetti: $12.0M revenue, $75.1M net loss, $99.9M cash (thin runway); D-Wave: $8.8M revenue; Oklo: zero revenue, $38.4M operating cash use, $275.3M cash plus securities (secondary); Plug Power: negative gross margin, equity-funded theme run.

patterns.pattern: Scale is not a barrier during a profit-pool shift. Even $100B mega caps 10x'd in about 16 months in the 2025-26 memory supercycle, so leader and candidate layers both matter.
patterns.evidence: SK hynix reported 'from $100 billion to $1 trillion in 16 months' (Invezz, 2026-05-27; market cap ₩1,680T on 2026-05-27); Micron topped $1T market cap on 2026-05-26 from FY2025 revenue of $37.38B; Sandisk, WDC and Lumentum rose several-fold from April 2025 lows (secondary).

patterns.pattern: Most 10-baggers have violent drawdowns or fundamental reversals afterward. Thematic or retail-driven runs especially need exit discipline.
patterns.evidence: EcoPro fell about 26% from peak within weeks in April 2023 amid Morgan Stanley and Samsung Securities valuation warnings (+848% YTD at the July 2023 peak); Rainbow Robotics later fell to roughly half its peak; Hanmi Q1 2026 sales -65.5% and operating profit -87.9% YoY after HBM second-sourcing; Micron retreated from a late-June 2026 peak above $1,200; Hanwha Aerospace Q3 2026 operating profit -46% YoY.
